title: Three-archetype inference tuning snapshot: batching, cache & quant suggestions
content:
Purpose
This is a compact working snapshot with concrete suggested settings for three representative workload archetypes so engineering + product can quickly convert into spreadsheet scenarios and validation runs. The goal is to propose settings that are safe to A/B in a canary, measurable in our cost model, and explicitly note quality risk vectors.

Scope / audience
- Audience: eng (serving runtime + infra), product-optimize, solutions eng
- Not a final playbook; a short, experiment-first set of recommendations to feed into the cost spreadsheet and rollout plan.

Workload archetypes and high-level priorities
1) Latency-sensitive interactive chat (Web/edge chat widget)
   - Priority: tail latency (p95/p99) and perceived interactivity. Cost matters but should not increase perceived delay.
   - Expected pattern: many short requests (avg prompt 40–80 tokens, gen 30–120 tokens), frequent session reuse, KV cache hit potential ~40–60% on repeated prompts.

2) High-throughput embedding pipeline (offline batch)
   - Priority: unit cost and throughput. Latency per item can be high (seconds) as long as throughput is maximized.
   - Expected pattern: large batches submitted via job queues, variable sequence lengths but typically <=512 tokens for document chunks.

3) Reranker / short-form generation (server-side mixed traffic)
   - Priority: balanced cost/latency and consistent quality for ranking. Requests are moderate-length, sometimes need deterministic outputs.
   - Expected pattern: small group reranking (k=5–20), repeated model cold starts for ad-hoc jobs.

Concrete suggested settings (per archetype)
- Notation: B = batch size (requests), L = max latency window (ms), Q = quantization profile, TTL = KV cache TTL (minutes)

1) Latency-sensitive interactive chat
   - Batch strategy: continuous batching with max B=8, L=10ms collection window for low-concurrency clients; dynamic envelope: if CPU/GPU utilization low allow B up to 16 but only for background users.
   - Max tokens per request cap: 512 prompt, 256 gen default; recommend per-route token caps enforced by API layer to prevent runaway batches.
   - KV cache policy: session-keyed prefix cache, TTL=60 minutes for active sessions, soft-evict if memory pressure >80%. Pre-cache top-10 prompt prefixes for power-users.
   - Quantization: conservative: int8 (dynamic) on Llama-family style models or fp16 when int8 path increases p99; flagging profile q=8 as default, q=4 (aggressive) only for non-critical routes.
   - Expected impact: ~25–40% cost reduction at steady state, p50 latency unchanged, p99 risk increase 5–15% depending on model/kernel choices.

2) High-throughput embedding pipeline
   - Batch strategy: bulk batching with target B=512–2048 items depending on vram; prefer fixed-size micro-batch groups (e.g., 256) aggregated into larger GPU batches for kernel efficiency.
   - Max latency window: L=2000ms (can be relaxed to 5s for heavy queueing).
   - Cache policy: dedupe identical input hashing + short-term result cache TTL=1440 minutes (24h) for re-ingestion protection; also use shard-local on-GPU embedding cache for last-N items when memory allows.
   - Quantization: aggressive quantization OK; recommend 4-bit (q4_k_m / awq-style) production path for encoder-only embedding models after regression checks. Use deterministic quant libs (GPTQ/AWQ) and keep fp16 fallback for validation runs.
   - Expected impact: 2x–4x cost reduction for embedding throughput when moving from fp16 to 4-bit with minimal vector similarity drift (<1% recall drop if validated).

3) Reranker / short-form generation
   - Batch strategy: grouped batching by job with B=32–128 depending on ranker k, asynchronous pipeline so rank scoring and fetching are overlapped.
   - Max latency window: L=50–150ms depending on SLA; use priority queue to avoid mixing critical requests with long background jobs.
   - Cache policy: keep per-job ephemeral KV cache for the lifetime of job (TTL=5 minutes) then evict; global prefix cache disabled to avoid stale context interactions.
   - Quantization: mixed: prefer int8 for forward pass; avoid 4-bit in top of ranker unless validated on held-out ranking set. Consider per-layer selective-quantization (first/last intact).
   - Expected impact: ~30–60% unit-cost saving with caution on small quality regressions for edge cases.

Suggested cost spreadsheet mapping keys (what to put into the model):
- Baseline: fp16, batch=1, no cache (per-route baseline numbers)
- Scenario A: conservative tuning (int8, safe batching, session cache) -> estimated cost delta column
- Scenario B: aggressive tuning (q4, large batches, long TTL caches for embeddings) -> estimated cost delta column
- Sensitivity columns: p50, p95, p99 latency deltas; quality metric deltas (embedding recall@k, reranker NDCG, chat ROUGE/acceptance proxy)

Validation plan and metrics to monitor in canary
- Metrics to collect: tokens/sec per GPU, cost-per-1M-tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, quality metrics per route (embedding similarity drift, reranker NDCG, chat-response-acceptance percent), error rates, tail OOMs, kernel fallback counts.
- Regression thresholds: fail canary if embedding recall@10 drops >1.5% absolute, reranker NDCG@10 drops >1.0% absolute, chat automated proxy score delta >2% or user-facing error increase >0.5%.
- Canary plan: progressive rollout 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 2x monitoring window per step (min 6 hours per step). Auto-rollback if any hard threshold breached.

Implementation notes (runtime ops)
- Prefer making quant profile a model variant in the model catalog so routing/rollback is simple (keep names like model-v1-fp16, model-v1-int8, model-v1-q4).
- Keep a synthetic microbench matrix in the spreadsheet: memory footprint / peak tokens / throughput at different batch sizes so infra autoscaler tuning can be automated.
- Add lightweight feature flag per route for cache TTLs so product can tune without code deploys.

Open questions / risks to resolve before wide rollout
- Kernel stability for q4 on particular model family (need kernel/regression test across our GPU fleet types).
- Quality drift measurement for chat: need a small human eval set for sensitive flows (N=300 examples minimum).
- Memory fragmentation and eviction behavior when mixing large embedding batches and interactive chat on same GPU pool.

Next steps (actionable)
- Product-optimize: convert these three rows into the cost spreadsheet and add baseline numbers (owner: Priya) by 2025-04-15.
- Eng-serving-runtime: add model-variant flags and a per-route TTL flag in the API layer (owner: Liam) - prototype by 2025-04-22.
- Applied-ML: run the validation matrix for q4 vs fp16 for the embedding model family and report delta table (owner: Aisha) by 2025-04-20.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive but conservative where user-perceived quality matters. Please comment inline on specific model families (e.g., Llama-2-70b) so we can pin exact quant libs.
- If you want alternate archetypes (edge-device, private-deploy on-prem), call that out and I will add an appendix with deployment-specific constraints.

Unresolved items to drop into JIRA
- JIRA-OPT-4322: q4 kernel validation across A100/4090 fleet
- JIRA-OPT-4323: human-eval set curation for chat-sensitive flows
- JIRA-OPT-4324: per-route TTL feature flag implementation

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Conservative defaults: int8 + small continuous batches + 60m session cache for chat.
- Aggressive path for batch embeddings: q4 + very large batches + long TTL caches for dedupe.
- Reranker: hybrid approach, avoid extreme 4-bit unless validated.
- Rollout slowly with automated rollback and tight regression thresholds.
